verdictBasis: The repairs select useful directions and remove several literal week-one choices: PlanIntent now has a domain-separated commitment and an AttemptRecord/ExecutionPlan/PlanId join, while storage now has one explicit projects/<ProjectId> ledger/CAS namespace. They are not seal-ready. The claimed closed PlanIntent admits malformed stage and contribution values, a stored-view intent cannot name its target or query, and DELIVERY has no closed v1 allow/deny matrix for several C-2-valid but slice-excluded forms. Storage consumes an undefined logical ProjectId, proves cross-project non-aliasing only as unequal path strings, and leaves crash recovery after full-project quarantine plus the cross-root authority switch unspecified. IP-R4-04 and IP-R4-06 therefore remain OPEN.

checkerResults.result: 11 PlanIntent, 7 intent-binding, 12 stage-plan and 6 Coverage fixtures reported clean
T1..T13 reported clean; publication remained BLOCKED
RI-PID and RI-JOIN reported clean; PLAN-ID-V1 remained IMPLEMENTABLE_UNEXECUTED
DL-SCOPE/DL-D9 reported clean; release remained NOT-DEMONSTRATED

independentProbes.method: Extract each ASCII-only fixture with jq -cjS, prepend the literal UTF-8 domain and NUL, and hash with the system SHA-256 implementation; neither check-c2.py nor its canonicaliser was used.
Mutate the valid minimal intent one field at a time and invoke the retained validator directly.
independentProbes.result: All six produced zero validation errors and a commitment. This contradicts PS-15's claim that malformed values reject before attempt admission.

The lifecycle and fixture consistently say no ExecutionId, AttemptRecord, ExecutionPlan or Run is created. However, the stored-view fixture is only the analysis fixture with admissionMode changed; PlanIntent contains no RunId, artifact ID, query, result noun, selector, or sealed-view commitment. The zero-attempt statement is internally consistent but the read request is not a closed executable request.

C-2 accepted one-field mutations selecting resident-single-project, resident-multi-project, repair, mutation, cloud-service, model-service, compilerPlugins=granted and projectHooks=granted. The v1 slice excludes those forms, but DELIVERY defines an exact selector/fixture only for external-scanner and a prose generic capability-runtime list. No closed overlay table assigns every C-2 enum/path to admit or an exact rejection outcome.

The positive field-13 commitment, projectId and logical stages agree, and the retained stage/project/commitment substitution fixtures reject. The join is not total over resolved admission data: PlanIntent contributions have four fields, PLAN-ID-V1 contributions have ten different/richer fields, top-level capabilityGrants exist only in PLAN-ID-V1, and check-resolved-inputs compares only activationId/contributionId pairs. The valid ExecutionPlan fixture's planIdentityInputs contains only planIntentCommitment rather than a closed thirteen-field descriptor.

independentProbes.axis: canonical ProjectId and physical cross-project non-aliasing
independentProbes.result: The lowercase path patterns and derived paths are exact. The checker defines alias as pathA == pathB. Adding equal physicalFileId values to the different-project fixture remained checker-clean, as did deleting logicalIdentityOwner and weakening the pre-existing-object collision rule. Thus the retained proof is lexical, not a physical file-identity/link test.

One ledger/WAL/SHM and one objects/sha256 tree per projects/<ProjectId> is unambiguous; root-level shared ledger/CAS and host-created cross-project hardlink/reflink/clone reuse are explicitly forbidden. This portion closes the literal root/ledger/CAS topology fork at SPECIFIED scope.

Project-local inventory and ordinary purge ownership are directionally clear. Replacing the entire fullProject quarantine rule with an untracked global quarantine remained checker-clean. The contract gives no quarantine path/identity/discovery rule after the canonical namespace is renamed, and no persistent authority-pointer/transaction that makes a switch between separately admitted roots atomic. Crash recovery and cross-root cutover therefore remain implementation choices.

The JSON contracts correctly remain SPECIFIED or IMPLEMENTABLE with IMPLEMENTABLE_UNEXECUTED evidence, empty product evidence, G5/G14 blocked, and publication blocked. The checker output does not demonstrate the product. The persistence narrative's SEALED storage heading and adjudications' no-week-one-fork language are premature while the independent findings below remain open.

positiveResults: All three PlanIntent commitment vectors independently reproduce exactly.
The PlanIntent domain tag, NUL framing, SHA-256 text form and PLAN-ID-V1 field-13 recipe agree.
Analysis-attempt commitment custody across frozen intent, AttemptRecord and ExecutionPlan is explicitly stated, and the retained basic substitution fixtures are meaningful.
stored-view-read is consistently specified as zero-attempt and zero-new-Run.
ProjectId/object text encodings reject traversal, case drift and alternate spellings.
The shared-root/projects/<ProjectId>/ledger.sqlite and project-local CAS choice is concrete, and within-project versus cross-project digest paths are distinct by construction.
Storage and admission assurance states do not claim qualification or demonstration.

findings.title: The closed PlanIntent shape does not close the value grammar and admits malformed authority-bearing plans
findings.statement: planIntent.schema closes top-level field names, but stageSchemas mostly closes only field presence. It does not bind JSON types, canonical ID forms, non-empty relation/rule sets, the requiredness enum spelling, dependency/reference types, or a budget grammar. The retained validator accepted null stage and contribution IDs, an unknown requiredness, empty required work sets and a negative untyped budget. This is not merely the acknowledged semantic-plan-lint limitation: PS-15 expressly says malformed values reject before ExecutionId.
findings.impact: Independent hosts can commit and admit different malformed objects, or fail at different later points after an attempt exists. The implementer must invent the actual Rust request types and validation boundary, so IP-R4-04's week-one API fork remains.
findings.requiredChange: Bind a closed value schema for every PlanIntent/stage/contribution field, including exact ID representations, REQUIRED/OPTIONAL wire values, non-empty/set/sequence rules, bounded integer budget units and reference validation. Add negative fixtures and mutations for each class and make PS-15 mechanically true.

findings.title: stored-view-read creates no attempt but cannot identify what sealed state to read
findings.statement: The stored-view fixture changes only admissionMode on an analysis intent. The closed PlanIntent has no RunId/view/artifact selector, query operation, result noun, expected retention state, or committed target identity. The blueprint's inspect_without_attempt receives only RequestContext and PlanIntent, so a real reader needs an uncommitted side channel or an implementation-invented interpretation of analysis stages.
findings.impact: The zero-attempt property is specified, but the request is not executable or substitution-safe. Two implementations can expose different stored-read APIs and commit different subsets while both satisfy the current fixture.
findings.requiredChange: Make the pre-admission request a closed tagged union, or add an exact StoredViewIntent payload containing the resolved sealed target and typed query/result selector. Commit it, require RequestId-only execution, and add positive/negative second-process read fixtures that prove target substitution cannot occur.

findings.title: Visibility exists, but the product overlay is not total over the v1 exclusion surface
findings.statement: C-2 deliberately represents resident topologies, repair/mutation workflows, cloud/model remote computation, compiler plugins and project hooks. v1-slice excludes them. DELIVERY binds an exact external-scanner selector and names several generic capability-runtime categories, but has no closed path/value allow/deny matrix or fixtures for the remaining enum values. All eight independent one-field examples were C-2-valid.
findings.impact: enforce_product_admission(intent) still requires an implementer-authored policy table. The same excluded request may be rejected pre-attempt, admitted, or assigned an invented reason depending on the implementation.
findings.requiredChange: Bind a closed v1 overlay over every PlanIntent exclusion-bearing path/value, including the exact allowed set, domain reason and existing D9 projection. Add one zero-attempt rejection fixture per excluded class and a checker that fails if a future C-2 enum value has no overlay disposition.

findings.title: The commitment equality omits exact contribution and grant records resolved before admission
findings.statement: PlanIntent commits contribution activationId/contributionId/origin/authority and per-stage grant names. PLAN-ID-V1 later commits contribution version, bundle, artifact digest, admission grant, role, verification state/evidence, parameters and separate versioned capability grants. AttemptRecord stores only planIntentCommitment, ExecutionPlan equality compares only project/stages/commitment, and the live cross-check compares only activationId/contributionId. No binding immutable admission descriptor joins the richer values to the pre-attempt decision.
findings.impact: An artifact, provenance outcome, parameter set or capability-grant record can differ after attempt admission while producing a newly valid PlanId, with no specified comparison to the exact values that were admitted. The host has to invent custody for resolved admission data.
findings.requiredChange: Either include the exact closed contribution/grant records in PlanIntent or commit a separately versioned AdmissionDescriptor stored atomically with AttemptRecord. Define ExecutionPlan.planIdentityInputs exactly and require full equality against the thirteen-field PlanDescriptor before snapshot/provider/stage use; add artifact/grant/parameter substitution vectors.

findings.title: The namespace fixes ProjectId text but no contract defines the logical ProjectId that supplies the 32 bytes
findings.statement: storageNamespace explicitly says it does not mint semantic project identity; C-2 only checks prj1- plus 64 lowercase hex; resolved-inputs defines root selection but no ProjectId recipe, persistence/custody, collision rule, clone/move behavior or supplied-versus-recomputed validation. No other reviewed binding surface closes that handoff.
findings.impact: The first resolver/store implementation must choose path-derived versus repository-derived versus persisted-random identity. That choice changes storage stability across moves/clones, collision/isolation behavior, backup/migration identity and whether two roots can accidentally share one ledger/CAS tenant.
findings.requiredChange: Add a binding PROJECT-ID-V1 owner/lifecycle/recipe or persisted allocation contract, canonical validation, collision and root-move/clone semantics, and positive/negative joins into C-2, storage admission and migration.

findings.title: The non-alias fixtures prove unequal path strings, not distinct physical files
findings.statement: validate_storage_fixture derives two strings and sets alias equal to pathA == pathB. It does not model file identity, link count, hardlink/reflink/clone state or a pre-existing object. An explicit same physical file ID on the two paths was ignored. The prose says OpenSIP writes independent files, but collision reuse only requires digest and same-project ledger ownership, and the checker remained green when that rule was weakened.
findings.impact: T13's physical-non-alias wording overstates the retained evidence. A later implementation or edit can reuse a cross-linked pre-existing file while the architecture checker remains green; G14 is correctly blocked but the design-integrity claim is not load-bearing.
findings.requiredChange: Narrow checker claims to lexical namespace integrity and add an implementation conformance property for regular-file identity/link count on publish and reuse, forbidden host-created clone/link operations, and cross-project equal-digest file identity. Keep product isolation undemonstrated until those controls run on each supported filesystem.

findings.category: full-project purge and migration state machine
findings.title: Quarantine recovery and cross-root authority cutover are not bound
findings.statement: fullProject requires a root-confined rename to a project-scoped purge quarantine, then deletion, but defines no quarantine path, identifier, root inventory rule, durable discovery record or crash-resume transition after the canonical projects/<ProjectId> path disappears. Migration says to atomically switch authority after copying to a separately admitted root, but defines neither the persistent authority pointer nor the transaction/rollback rule that makes a cross-root switch atomic. The checker ignores fullProject entirely and validates migration/purge mainly by substrings.
findings.impact: A crash after namespace rename can orphan user-derived bytes outside canonical inventory, and two implementations can select different source/target authorities after interrupted migration. These are precisely inventory/purge/migration choices the adjudication claims to close.
findings.requiredChange: Bind exact quarantine placement/naming, root inventory discovery, journal custody and crash state transitions; bind the authority-selection record and copy/verify/switch/rollback protocol for cross-root migration. Add executable transition fixtures for every crash point and checker mutations that alter those fields.

findings.title: The shared implementer and status surfaces have not converged on the candidate contracts
findings.statement: The adjudications correctly say shared integration is pending. IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT still depicts indexes/<fact-view-id> rather than the binding cache namespace and omits the root marker; architecture/06 labels storage ownership SEALED while the live TM contract and freeze draft require independent rereview. The binding JSON wins, but the implementation package is the week-one consumer.
findings.impact: An implementer following the package instead of recursively reconciling artifacts can create a storage-schema-major divergence on day one, and process status can present an unreviewed repair as sealed.
findings.requiredChange: After substantive repairs pass rereview, update the blueprint/freeze/narrative and claim register in one serialized integration change, then rerun link, checker and completeness verification.

IP-R4-04.why: The representation and base commitment/equality direction are useful, but R7-C2-01 through R7-C2-04 leave the executable request grammar, stored-read request, complete product overlay and exact admitted-input equality open.

IP-R4-06.why: The project-local path/ledger/CAS topology is selected, but R7-SN-01 through R7-SN-03 leave logical ProjectId identity, physical non-alias conformance and crash-safe purge/migration authority open.

assuranceAssessment.forbiddenInference: Normal checks and mutation selftests establish only that the current selected fields and retained mutations are internally guarded. They neither answer the independent probes nor qualify physical storage/admission behavior.
assuranceAssessment.narrativeCorrectionRequired: Do not mark storage ownership or IP-R4-04/IP-R4-06 sealed until the open review findings are adjudicated and the shared implementation package is synchronized.

minimumBeforeRereview: A closed typed PlanIntent/StoredViewIntent wire schema with exact ID/enums/non-empty/budget/reference rules and new negative controls.
A total v1 product overlay table covering every C-2 value and exact pre-attempt outcome.
A full immutable admission-data join into AttemptRecord, ExecutionPlan and PLAN-ID-V1, with artifact/grant/parameter substitutions rejected.
A binding logical ProjectId identity/lifecycle contract joined to root resolution and migration.
A physical-file non-alias implementation property plus checker-honest lexical claims.
Exact full-project quarantine recovery and cross-root migration authority-switch state machines.
Serialized implementer-package, narrative and register convergence followed by full normal/selftest verification.

resolves.note: This independent review records evidence and findings only. It does not adjudicate, repair, seal or update shared coordination surfaces.
